ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
Anna has four discs of different sizes. She wants to build a tower using 3 discs. A smaller disc always has to lie on top of a bigger disc. How many ways are there for Anna to build this tower?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: In the image, it can be seen that there are a total of 4 disks, and their sizes are all different. The problem text states that Anna wants to use 3 of the disks to build a tower, and a small disk must be placed on top of a large disk. Therefore, once any 3 disks are selected, their top-bottom order is uniquely determined by the size rule and cannot be arranged arbitrarily again. So the problem only needs to calculate the number of ways to choose 3 from 4 different disks: C(4,3)=4.
